Decision: Description List handled via global styles rather than a dedicated component.
Rationale: Native <dl> / <dt> / <dd> elements are sufficient. A dedicated component would add complexity without clear benefit given uncertain usage in the Dashboard.
Impact on Current System: Style <dl> elements in the global CSS layer. No Description List component will be built in v3.

Decision: Tabs split into two separate components: Tabs (Navigation) and Tabs (Panel).
Rationale: Navigation tabs and panel tabs share a visual design but have fundamentally different markup and behavior. Navigation tabs are link-based (<nav> + <a>) and CSS-only. Panel tabs require the ARIA tablist/tabpanel pattern and React. Only the navigation variant is currently used in VIP — panel tabs are deferred.
Impact on Current System: Build Tabs (Navigation) as CSS-only in v3. Defer Tabs (Panel) until a use case arises.

Decision: Table built as a simple CSS-only styled display table in v3.
Rationale: VIP plans to replace all table usage with a more complex table component from another design system. Building a full-featured data table now would be wasted effort. A simple styled table covers current display needs in the interim.
Impact on Current System: Build Table as CSS-only in v3. Plan for migration to third-party table component as part of broader a8c design system adoption.

Decision: Tile documented as a pattern rather than built as a component.
Rationale: Usage is speculative — Tile exists in Figma but is not currently used in the Dashboard. Building a component without a real use case risks designing an API that doesn't fit actual needs. Row-level states (hover, disabled) could justify a component eventually, but the variable right-side control makes the API tricky. Option Row may evolve into Tile if a concrete use case arises.
Impact on Current System: Document Tile as a pattern in Phase 7. Revisit as a component candidate when a real Dashboard use case is identified.

Decision: Status Indicator deferred from v3 scope.
Rationale: No current use case identified in the Dashboard. Building it now without a real consumer would risk designing for a hypothetical rather than an actual need.
Impact on Current System: Defer until a concrete Dashboard use case arises. Add to v3 scope at that point.

Decision: Chart Card included in the design system as a shell/frame component.
Rationale: Chart Card provides layout chrome (title, description, link, action buttons, chart slot) without owning any chart library. The chart slot is exposed via a children prop so the Dashboard can render Recharts or any other library inside it. children prop chosen over a fixed-height placeholder for flexibility — if layout consistency becomes hard to maintain this way, consider switching to a fixed-height slot with a configurable height prop.
Impact on Current System: Build Chart Card as a React organism. Design system owns chrome and layout only. Dashboard is responsible for chart content.

Decision: Stat Card included in the design system.
Rationale: Stat Card (Card + Stat + optional link/actions) has no dependency on Recharts or any chart library. It was initially excluded as Dashboard-specific but reinstated once it was clear no chart library is required.
Impact on Current System: Build Stat Card as a React organism.

Decision: Sparkline excluded from the design system as a component.
Rationale: Sparkline is a data visualization component built with Recharts — a third-party charting library. Data visualization components are tightly coupled to their data shape, chart library API, and Dashboard-specific context (Health/Metrics section), making them poor candidates for a general-purpose design system component. The design system's role is to provide tokens and styles that consuming apps use to build their own data visualizations consistently.
Impact on Current System: Sparkline stays in the Dashboard as a Recharts component. Update hardcoded GOLD color constants to reference design system tokens when the Dashboard adopts v3.

Decision: Environment Switcher excluded from the design system as a component.
Rationale: Too tightly coupled to VIP's environment concept to be a reusable design system component. The design system will provide tokens and block styles to support it, but the component itself belongs in the VIP Dashboard.
Impact on Current System: Environment Switcher component lives in the Dashboard, not the design system. Revisit during Phase 5 to confirm token and style coverage in the design system is sufficient.

Decision: Confirmation Dialog merged into Dialog as a variant rather than a separate component.
Rationale: No behavior in Confirmation Dialog justifies a separate component — it is a smaller focused variant of Dialog.
Impact on Current System: Remove NewConfirmationDialog imports in the Dashboard and replace with Dialog using the confirmation variant.

Decision: Date Picker implementation approach deferred to Phase 5.
Rationale: Radix does not have a Date Picker primitive. React Day Picker is a strong candidate — it handles calendar grid, keyboard navigation, and ARIA without imposing styles, which would save significant effort over a full custom build. Needs evaluation before committing to an approach.
Impact on Current System: Evaluate React Day Picker before Phase 5 implementation begins. If adopted, it replaces a full custom build for the calendar grid and date logic.

Decision: Code component removed from v3 scope.
Rationale: No clear use case identified in the VIP Dashboard — Console covers all current monospace display needs. Code can be added in a future version if a need arises.
Impact on Current System: None — Code is not currently used in the Dashboard in a way that differs from Console.

Decision: ButtonSubmit removed as a separate component. Replaced by native <button type=""submit""> with appropriate variant styling.
Rationale: ButtonSubmit has no behavior beyond being a submit button. Native HTML handles this without a wrapper component.
Impact on Current System: Remove ButtonSubmit imports in the Dashboard and replace with <button type=""submit"">.

Decision: Combined Autocomplete and AutocompleteMulti into a single component with a multiple prop.
Rationale: Shared logic (filtering, keyboard navigation, dropdown, ARIA combobox pattern) is substantial enough to warrant a single implementation. The visual difference (chips rendered inside the input field for multi mode) is handled internally by the component based on the prop.
Impact on Current System: AutocompleteMulti usage in the Dashboard will need to be updated to <Autocomplete multiple> at each call site.

Decision: Icon system uses @boxicons/core with an SVG sprite compiled at build time.
Rationale: Boxicons is the icon set already used in Figma. The core package provides raw SVGs (viewBox 0 0 24 24, currentColor, no hardcoded dimensions) — the ideal format for a design system. An SVG sprite (compiled from the core package's svg/ directory) is preferred over the Boxicons icon font and over @boxicons/react. Font icons have accessibility and rendering quality problems. React-only icons would leave CSS-only components without icon support. An SVG sprite works in plain HTML, inherits currentColor for theming, is tree-shakable per-sprite, and is framework-agnostic. Icons are referenced with <svg class="icon"><use href="#bx-{name}"/></svg> and an .icon utility class controls size via 1em so icons scale with surrounding text.
Impact on Current System: Add Phase 4.5 to the build plan. Install @boxicons/core. Add sprite build step to npm run build. Add .icon utility class. Document usage pattern in Storybook.

Decision: Icons sized in cap units (1cap) with a .with-icon composition for placement, following Every Layout’s Icon.
Rationale: 1em is the font size, not the letter height: at 16px an em-sized icon is 16px against a cap height of 11.27px — 42% taller than the capitals beside it. 1cap matches cap height so icons optically align with text. A 0.75em fallback is declared first for browsers without cap support (within 6.5% of true cap height). Placement uses inline-flex with align-items: baseline rather than vertical-align, so the icon sits on the text baseline like a capital letter. The .with-icon gap is em-relative rather than a --space-* token so it scales with surrounding text — a deliberate exception to the space scale. Controls that centre their contents (.button, .toolbar) keep align-items: center and use the .icon sizing without .with-icon.
Impact on Current System: Supersedes the 1em sizing in Phase 4.5 step 35. Adds step 35a for .with-icon. Applies when the icon branch (worktree-agent-af28894adf4280bce) is merged — its icon.css currently uses 1em and vertical-align: middle, both of which need replacing.
